Subject: On‑prem order form + operator obligations — initial materials

Hi Mateo / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and IT at Canyon want to start locking in commercial terms and the operational exhibits for the on‑prem order form. Two immediate asks:

1) Can you confirm what evidence/stewardship Redwood can commit to for an on‑prem (customer‑hosted) deployment — specifically: snapshot retention, witness options, and operator access windows?
2) We need a version of Exhibit A that reflects the licensed runtime boundary and any derivative rights carveouts so our legal team can map to our internal audit.

I've attached the OrderForm_CCN_v1.docx with the customer fields filled and a short procurement checklist. We prefer a light escrow or witness model (snapshot deposit + one witness session per year) for now, but we are open to alternatives if you can show equivalent assurance.

Can you loop in Legal and Ops folks and propose next steps / dates? We are targeting an internal procurement signoff by 11/15.

Thanks,
Amelia Reyes
Sr. Sourcing Manager | Canyon Clinical
amelia.reyes@canyonclinical.com

Subject: Re: On‑prem order form + operator obligations — initial materials

Amelia — thanks for the clear asks and the Order Form. Looping in Legal (David) and Infra/Deploy (Kim) to confirm feasibility. Quick responses and proposed next steps below: 

- Evidence/stewardship: Redwood can provide periodic encrypted forensic snapshots and a time‑boxed witness session. We need to clarify retention windows (default 90 days vs customer required 365 days) because longer retention has implications for storage/forensics SLA and cost.
- Operator access windows: we can provide temporary access tokens for a supervised witness session or run witnessless verification where we hand over signed provenance manifests and a snapshot hash.
- Exhibit A: we'll prepare a draft addendum that enumerates the licensed runtime boundary (model binaries vs inference artifacts), and proposed derivative rights language for review.

Proposed timeline:
- 11/02: Redwood sends redline draft of MSA Addendum + Exhibit A
- 11/04: 30‑minute legal sync to walk boarder items (David + Canyon legal)
- 11/08: Ops deep dive on witness/runbook (Kim + Tom)

If that works, David will attach redlines and Kim will attach the operator obligations matrix. Let me know if you want a different cadence.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Exec, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: amelia.reyes@canyonclinical.com; mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com; kimberly_park@redwood.com; canyon-legal@canyonclinical.com
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 09:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem order form + operator obligations — redlines attached

Amelia / team,

Thanks — attached are Redwood's initial redlines for the MSA addendum and a draft operator obligations matrix: MSA_Addendum_ExhibitA_redlines.docx; operator_obligations_matrix.xlsx. High‑level notes:

1) License boundary: our position is that Redwood licenses the runtime and model artifacts required to serve the customer workload; customer retains data and customer‑payload‑derived outputs. We proposed language to limit derivative rights to customer output only (no carveout for reproducing model weights).
2) Snapshot custody: we can provide encrypted snapshots for verification. We cannot leave keys or raw images in a third‑party escrow without a clear legal framework; propose a sealed snapshot deposit with HSM‑backed key escrow (Redwood retains custody of encryption keys unless a mutually agreed exception is engaged).
3) Witnessing: we can support either (A) a supervised witness session at customer site with temporary console access + RBAC scope, or (B) a witnessless verification path: signed manifest + reproducible test runs on a seeded dataset. The witnessless path is operationally lighter but requires a fixed test harness to be accepted by your auditors.
4) Audit window & retention: redlines propose a 90‑day default retention with an option for extended retention for an incremental cost.

Questions for Canyon Legal (cc'd):
- Would the sealed snapshot deposit + Redwood‑held HSM keys satisfy your internal forensic chain‑of‑custody needs, or do you require an independent escrow steward?
- Are there specific forensic artifacts (e.g., Docker images, VM snapshots, model checkpoints) you regard as mandatory evidence items?

If helpful I'll join the 11/04 legal sync.

Regards,
David Kim
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
attachments: MSA_Addendum_ExhibitA_redlines.docx, operator_obligations_matrix.xlsx
From: Canyon Clinical Legal <canyon-legal@canyonclinical.com>

Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem order form + operator obligations — follow up and preferences

David / Mateo — thanks for the redlines. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Independent escrow steward: our compliance team strongly prefers an independent escrow steward for sealed snapshots rather than vendor‑held keys. The steward's role would be limited to holding an encrypted snapshot and releasing to both parties under agreed conditions (e.g., bankruptcy, breach).
- Mandatory artifacts: our auditors will expect (i) snapshot of runtime image, (ii) cryptographic manifest of installed packages, (iii) a short execution log demonstrating ability to reproduce inference results on a seeded test case.
- Witnessing: we prefer a hybrid approach — a witnessless verification in normal operations, supplemented by an annual witnessing window with a visiting engineer (or witness session via secure screen share) for critical releases.

We reviewed your proposed derivative language; we need one minor change to ensure the license doesn't permit Redwood to redistribute model checkpoints to third parties. We'll propose exact language in the 11/04 legal sync.

Also: we opened a DocuSign pre‑fill for the order form and attached a compliance checklist in the shared Drive. Link: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=demo&acct=12345

— Canyon Clinical Legal
